Work / ER Command

Hackathon demo

ER Command

An emergency-room operations screen that reads handwritten notes in English, Urdu and Roman Urdu.

Source on GitHub →
Context
Built at AICON'26, NUST
Type
Web app with AI document reading
Stack
Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Gemini
Status
Working demo with made-up data

The problem

Emergency rooms in Pakistan run on ambulance slips, referral notes and handwritten charts written in English, Urdu and Roman Urdu. When the shift changes, things get missed: a drip that is 90 minutes late, a critical patient with no doctor, a corridor full of trolleys.

What we built

Reads the paperworkGemini extracts patients and care tasks from photos of slips and charts, in three languages.
Rules decide, not the AIFixed ESI triage rules set who goes first. The AI only reads; it never makes the clinical call.
One screen for the shiftWho is waiting, which tasks are late, free beds and busy doctors, updated live.
Handover briefA short summary the charge nurse can read aloud, in English or Urdu.

How it works

Staff photograph or type an arrival. The model turns it into structured fields; code then scores urgency with fixed rules, assigns tasks with owners and due times, and raises an alarm when anything is overdue. A surge mode drops fifteen arrivals at once to stress-test the queue.

Status, honestly

This is a hackathon build, shown here with made-up data and the AI switched off so anyone can try it. It is not in use at a hospital. It shows how we build: AI for the messy reading, plain rules for the decisions that matter.
